capitals.name: Kharkiv (Kharkov)
capitals.note: Infobox capital 1919-1934; the Soviet government of December 1917 and the constitution of 10 March 1919 were also at Kharkiv. In November 1918 the Provisional Workers' and Peasants' Government of Ukraine was created in Kursk.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Soviet Ukrainian government was founded at Kharkiv on 24-25 December 1917, but the pages give no territory; Cliopatria draws Ukraine inside the Russian Republic. The shape is a radius around Kharkiv (the page names no other city). In 1918 the Central Powers and the Kiev UNR held the country and the Soviet government was recreated at Kursk on 28 November 1918. The ledger now carries the January-March 1918 gains (Yekaterinoslav 9 January, Aleksandrovsk 15 January, Poltava 20 January, Kiev 9 February) and the loss of Kiev on 1 March 1918 and of the rest by spring (confidence 1), all from the Ukrainian-Soviet War page; the shape stays the Kharkiv radius for the year.

correction.text: the Soviet-held part of Ukraine east of the Riga line: without Galicia and Volhynia (Poland), Northern Bukovina and Budjak (Romania) and Carpathian Ruthenia (Czechoslovakia); the Crimea (RSFSR) is not part of the Natural Earth country

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 469,382 km2, for 1919-1920: modern Ukraine without the west (Galicia, Volhynia), Northern Bukovina and Budjak, Carpathian Ruthenia and the Crimea. This is the Soviet claim at its spring-1919 maximum, not control for the whole of 1919-1920: the ledger now carries the gains from the Ukrainian People's Republic (January-March 1919), the losses to South Russia (the Donbas in May, Kharkov 25 June, Yekaterinoslav 30 June, Poltava 31 July, Odesa 23 August, Kyiv 31 August 1919), the regains (Kharkov and Sumy in December 1919, the rest of Ukraine by early 1920) and the loss and regain of Zhytomyr and Kiev to Poland (26 April-June 1920), so the claim no longer double-draws south-russia's 1919 keyframe or Poland's hold of Kiev. The infobox gives 603,700 km2 with no year (the 1954-1991 republic). The Moldavian ASSR (1924-1940) beyond the Dniester is not drawn.

correction.text: the Soviet-held part of Ukraine east of the Riga line: without Galicia and Volhynia (Poland), Northern Bukovina and Budjak (Romania) and Carpathian Ruthenia (Czechoslovakia); the Crimea (RSFSR) is not part of the Natural Earth country

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 469,382 km2, for 1921-1938: the same shape as 1919-1920 now held in full after the Treaty of Riga (18 March 1921) fixed the western border about 250 km east of the Curzon Line; Galicia and Volhynia went to Poland, Northern Bukovina and Budjak to Romania, Carpathian Ruthenia to Czechoslovakia, and the Crimea stayed with the RSFSR. The Moldavian ASSR (1924-1940) beyond the Dniester is not drawn.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 562,702 km2: Western Ukraine annexed in November 1939; "the Soviet Union secured almost all Polish territory east of the line of the rivers Pisa, Narew, Western Bug and San" (28 September 1939), about 200,000 km2 for the three republics together. The shape holds from November; before it use the 1919 keyframe.

correction.text: with Northern Bukovina, Hotin and Budjak (August 1940)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 583,693 km2: "the republic increased its territory to 560,000 sq km" (Ukrainian SSR page, about the 1939-1940 annexations); Hertsa, Northern Bukovina, Hotin, Ismail and Cetatea Alba counties assigned to Ukraine on 2 August 1940. During 1941-1944 the republic was occupied (ledger occupation events), not abolished.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 623,651 km2 against the infobox 603,700 km2 (ratio 0.97): the Crimean Oblast transferred by decree of 19 February 1954. Sevastopol "never formally ratified the transfer" and was attached to the oblast only in 1978; it is drawn with the Crimea here.

ledger.note: 1917, 24-25 December: the Soviet government of Ukraine is founded at Kharkiv, rival of the Kiev-based Ukrainian People's Republic: "The government of the Ukrainian Soviet Republic was founded on 24-25 December 1917."

1918, January: Bolshevik forces advance on Kiev, taking "Yekaterinoslav (January 9), Aleksandrovsk (January 15), and Poltava (January 20)" after Kharkov (26 December 1917). [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event; the 1917 keyframe is only the Kharkiv radius, and the reviewer asked for the 1918 gains and loss.]

1918, 9 February: the Bolshevik forces "entered Kiev under Mikhail Muravyov's [command] on February 9"; on the same day the UNR signed the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk with the Central Powers. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event.]

1918, 1 March: the combined forces "retook Kiev on March 1", "pushing the Bolsheviks out of Right Bank Ukraine" (the Ukrainian War of Independence page: "Kyiv was taken on 1 March by a force of 450,000 German troops"); the counterpart is the German Empire as the lead of the Central Powers' force, with the UNR. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event: the 1918 loss to the Central Powers.]

region.text: the rest of the Soviet holdings of early 1918

ledger.note: 1918, spring: the rest of the Soviet-held land (Kharkov, Poltava, Yekaterinoslav, Aleksandrovsk) passes to the Central Powers. Bridging: the Ukrainian-Soviet War page's account of the 1918 occupation stops at Kiev (1 March) and does not cover Kharkov in April; the evidence is that the Soviet government is recreated at Kursk, outside Ukraine, on 28 November 1918 (capital_move below). The month is a placeholder inside March-November 1918. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event, confidence 1.]

1918, 28 November: the Provisional Workers' and Peasants' Government of Ukraine is created at Kursk, outside Ukraine, while the Central Powers and the UNR hold the country; the seat returns to Kharkiv in 1919.
1919, 3 January: "On January 3, the Red Army took Kharkov." [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event: the winter 1918-1919 offensive that restores the republic's land.]
1919, January: "On January 20 the Soviet Army took Poltava" and "on January 26 Dybenko took Yekaterinoslav". [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event.]

1919, 5 February: Kyiv "fell to the Red Army again on 5 February" (the Ukrainian-Soviet War page: the Directorate was forced to Vinnytsia on 2 February and "troops of Schors and Bozhenko occupied Kiev three days later"). [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event.]

1919, 10 March: the Third All-Ukrainian Congress of Soviets at Kharkiv ratifies the constitution of the Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic, the republic "itself" being proclaimed on this date (infobox); the state of December 1917 continues.

ledger.note: 1919, early: "a new, swift Bolshevik offensive overran most of Eastern and central Ukraine in early 1919" (Ukrainian War of Independence page; no dates for Odesa, Kherson, Chernihiv and the other oblasts). Region is the 1919 keyframe minus the cities dated above; month is the researcher's reading of 'early 1919'. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event: this is the gain that explains the growth from the Kharkiv radius of 1917-1918 to the 1919 keyframe.]

1919, May: the AFSR offensive forces the Red Southern Front back, and the Denikin page has Denikin's forces checking a major Red offensive in the Donbas and routing the Red armies in May; the pages give no day for the Donbas. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: mirror of the south-russia gain.]

1919, 25 June: "On 25 June 1919, Denikin's Armed Forces of South Russia captured Kharkov, followed by Ekaterinoslav on 30 June." The Southern Front page has only the May offensive forcing the front to leave Kharkov. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: was May 1919 from the Southern Front page, which dates the offensive, not the capture; mirror of the south-russia gain.]
1919, 30 June: Denikin's forces captured Kharkov on 25 June, "followed by Ekaterinoslav on 30 June". [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event; mirror of the south-russia gain.]
1919, 31 July: "He took Poltava on July 31, Odesa on August 23, and Kyiv on August 31" (Kenez, quoted on the page). [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event; mirror of the south-russia gain.]

1919, 23 August: Denikin "took ... Odesa on August 23" (Kenez, quoted); the Southern Front page lists Odessa among the cities the front gave up between August and October. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event; mirror of the south-russia gain. The UkrSSR page adds that in August 1919 Lenin ordered the liquidation of the second Soviet Ukrainian government.]

1919, 31 August: "... and Kyiv on August 31" (Kenez, quoted on the page); the Ukrainian-Soviet War page agrees ("on 31 August Anton Denikin's Volunteer Army established its positions in the city"); the Southern Front page puts the front's loss of Kiev between August and October. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: was year-only (1919) and sorted before the March and May events; now month 8 and moved after the Poltava loss.]

1920, winter: "by 1920 all of Eastern and central Ukraine except Crimea was again in Bolshevik hands" (Ukrainian War of Independence page). Bridging: no page opened dates Kiev, Poltava, Yekaterinoslav or Odessa between December 1919 and February 1920; dated to the January-March 1920 collapse of South Russia. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: mirror of south-russia /ledger/18 (confidence 1, flagged).]

ledger.note: 1920, 25 April: "The Kiev Expedition, in which 65,000 Polish and 15,000 Ukrainian soldiers took part, commenced on 25 April 1920"; Zhytomyr was captured on 26 April, Kiev entered on 7 May. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: was year-only 1920 at confidence 1 (Treaty of Riga page); the Kiev offensive page dates it. The zone now includes the Kiev region.]
1920, 26 April: "Zhytomyr was captured on 26 April" by the Polish-Ukrainian forces. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event.]

1920, 7 May: "The combined Polish-Ukrainian forces under General Rydz-Smigly entered the city on 7 May." The Polish offensive stopped at Kiev and the front formed along the Dnieper (Ukrainian-Soviet War page: a Ukrainian division under Bezruchko entered Kiev on 7 May). [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event.]

1920, June: the Soviet counteroffensive (28 May; the 1st Cavalry Army broke through on 5 June and reached Zhytomyr and Berdychiv by 7 June) forces the Poles out: "After 10 June, Rydz-Smigly evacuated the 3rd Polish Army from Kiev. The Soviets were back." The page gives no day for the Soviet return. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event: the regain.]

1920, June: "In June 1920, Wrangel launched his last major offensive, the Northern Taurida Operation" and "his forces broke out of the Crimean bottleneck and captured a large territory to the north" (Pyotr Wrangel page; the page names no towns). Northern Taurida (Zaporizhzhya and Kherson oblasts) lies inside this republic's shape; no page says which republic administered it in 1920. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event, mirror of the south-russia gain (the RSFSR's Natural Earth shape does not contain the land).]

1920, 28 October to 3 November: the Red Southern Front's "counteroffensive in northern Taurida between 28 October and 3 November" captured Perekop, Henichesk, Melitopol and Chongar. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new event, mirror of the south-russia loss.]

ledger.note: 1921, 18 March: the Treaty of Riga ends the Polish-Soviet War; the border runs about 250 km east of the Curzon Line, Poland recognises Soviet Ukraine and Belarus and withdraws recognition from the Ukrainian People's Republic, and western Ukraine goes to Poland.

1922, 30 December: Ukraine joins the USSR "along with the Russian, Byelorussian and Transcaucasian republics" as a founding republic; it keeps its territory and becomes an internal unit of the Union (union-of-soviet-socialist-republics).

ledger.note: 1940, 2 August: the Moldavian SSR is formed from six Bessarabian counties and the westernmost part of the autonomous republic (about 4,118 km2), "effectively dissolving it"; the page is silent on the rest of the territory, which the infobox lists as Moldova and Ukraine today, so it is drawn as returning to the Ukrainian SSR. region.text: western Ukraine, the Right Bank west of Kiev and the south

ledger.note: 1941, June: "Immediately after the start of German-Soviet War in June 1941" the Germans enter; "On 29 June 1941 OUN members launched an uprising in Lviv" and the next day "after the entry of German troops" Stetsko proclaimed the Ukrainian state; "By 10 July 1941, German forces found themselves on distant approaches to Kyiv"; Lviv, Drohobych, Stanislaviv and Ternopil oblasts are incorporated into the General Governorate, and right-bank Ukraine goes to the Reichskommissariat Ukraine. Confidence 3 for Lviv; the other oblasts of this group are dated only by the campaign and the grouping is the researcher's reading. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: the whole-country occupation dated October 1941 is split by stage as the reviewer asked: the west and the Right Bank from June 1941 (this event), the Left Bank and the Kiev region by October 1941, Luhansk on 27 July 1942.]

region.text: Northern Bukovina, Budjak and Odesa with its surroundings

ledger.note: 1941, 26 July: Romanian and German troops complete the occupation of Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina; Izmail and Chernivtsi oblasts are attached to Romania, Odesa and the surrounding area becomes the Transnistria Governorate (UkrSSR page; the page gives no day).

region.text: the Left Bank and the Kiev region

ledger.note: 1941, by October: "By October, the Germans had captured Kharkiv and Stalino." Confidence 2: the page dates Kharkiv and Stalino (Donetsk) by October; the Kiev region and the rest of the Left Bank fell earlier in the campaign, but no page opened dates them, so October is an upper bound for this group. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: the former whole-country event, split by stage.]

1942, 27 July: "On 27 July 1942 last Soviet troops retreated from Shchotove in Luhansk Oblast, signifying the occupation of the whole territory of Soviet Ukraine by Nazi Germany." [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new stage event.]

1943, December 1942 to February 1943: "between December 1942 and February 1943 Soviet forces expelled German troops from easternmost parts of Ukraine up to the Mius river"; the page gives no month for Luhansk Oblast. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new stage event.]

region.text: the Left Bank and the Kiev region

ledger.note: 1943, 6 November: "in Autumn 1943 Soviet armies advanced to the Dnieper, and on 6 November entered Kyiv"; the page gives no dates for Kharkiv, the other Left Bank oblasts or Zaporizhzhya and Dnipropetrovsk (earlier and later in 1943). [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: new stage event; the date is the page's one anchor for the group.]

1944, early: "In early 1944, the Soviet Union gradually took over the territory through the Uman-Botosani and Second Jassy-Kishinev offensives" (Bessarabia page); the Ukrainian SSR page has "In April armies of the 3rd Ukrainian Front took Odesa" (year implied by the context). The page gives no day for Chernivtsi or Izmail, and the final collapse of the Axis front at Jassy-Kishinev is August 1944. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: was August 1944; the Bessarabia page says the Soviet Union took the territory over in early 1944, and Odesa fell in April.]

region.text: western Ukraine, the Right Bank west of Kiev and the south

ledger.note: 1944, by October: "the Germans were driven out of Ukraine between February 1943 and October 1944" and "by 28 October 1944 expelled German troops from Transcarpathia". Bridging: the page dates no oblast of this group (Lviv, Zhytomyr, Vinnytsya, Mykolayiv and the others fell between late 1943 and the summer of 1944); October 1944 is the page's last date for the whole country. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: the former whole-country end, kept for the western group.]
1945, 29 June: "Czechoslovakia officially agreed to transfer Carpathian Ruthenia to the Ukrainian SSR."

1954, 19 February: the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet decrees the transfer of the Crimean Oblast from the Russian SFSR to the Ukrainian SSR (RSFSR amendment 2 June, Ukrainian amendment 17 June 1954). Sevastopol "never formally ratified the transfer".
1991, 24 August: Ukraine declares independence on the dissolution of the Soviet Union; the republic of 603,700 km2 becomes Ukraine (referendum 1 December, recognition 26 December 1991).

notes: No Cliopatria row: Cliopatria draws Soviet Ukraine inside the Russian Republic (1917-1919), Republics of the Soviet Union (1920-1921) and USSR shapes, with a Ukrainian People's Republic row for 1919 only; the renderer should treat this dossier as an internal unit of the USSR. Exceeded the 5-page budget by two pages (Southern Front and Denikin, shared with the South Russia dossier). Not settled: (1) the 1918-1920 territory, on which the pages give no extents; (2) the Moldavian ASSR (12 October 1924 to 2 August 1940) is now a vassal in the ledger, but the page lists no districts and says nothing of what happened to the rest of its land in 1940, and the transfers of the Donbas, Taganrog and Kuban lands with Russia in the 1920s are not on the pages opened; (3) the dates of liberation of Kharkiv (1943) and Kiev (1943) are not on the page, so the occupation_end is placed at 28 October 1944 at confidence 2; (4) the 1945 Polish border treaty and the 1947 Paris treaty (Izmail) are not on the pages. The infobox starts the state in December 1917 but the republic itself is dated 10 March 1919. Counterparts needing dossiers: Second Polish Republic (eu-21), Kingdom of Romania, Nazi Germany, Czechoslovakia (those exist); Moldavian SSR and Moldavian ASSR (written, this batch), Byelorussian SSR (this batch), Crimean ASSR, South Russia (this batch).
